title: Technology Sector Update for 06/15/2018: JBL,QCOM,NXPI,FIT
text:

Technology stocks were declining Friday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing almost 0.5% while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a nearly 0.4% decrease.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- Jabil Circuit ( JBL ) retreated Friday, sliding as much as 10%, although the contract manufacturer reported fiscal Q3 financial results exceeding Wall Street estimates. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.46 per share compared with a $0.31 per share non-GAAP profit during the same quarter last year and topping the Capital IQ consensus by $0.02 per share. Revenue rose to $5.44 billion from $4.49 billion during the year-ago period, also easily surpassing the $4.90 billion Street view. Jabil is projecting adjusted Q4 net income in a range of $0.56 to $0.80 per share on $5.2 billion to $5.6 billion in revenue, in line with forecasts for a non-GAAP profit of $0.68 per share on $5.2 billion in revenue. It also authorized the repurchase of up to $350 million of its shares through Aug. 31, 2019.
In other sector news:
- Qualcomm ( QCOM ) was swinging between small gains and losses during Friday trading after the specialty chipmaker again extended the cash tender period for its proposed buyout of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ) by another week until next Thursday, June 22, at 5 p.m. ET. Through the most recent deadline Thursday night, NXP investors had tendered slightly more than 16.3 million of their shares, representing about 4.7% of the rival chipmaker's outstanding stock, down from around 17.7 million shares tendered on June 7.
- Fitbit ( FIT ) slumped about 3% on Friday after six current and former employees of the wearable technology company were charged with stealing trade secrets from a now-defunct rival. The indictment filed Thursday by the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of California in San Jose accuses the Fitbit employees of receiving trade secrets from Jawbone without authorization after leaving the company. Jawbone previously also accused Fitbit of a 2015 clandestine effort to steal talent, trade secrets and intellectual property before agreeing to a December 2017 settlement..
